prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the near ground from the more distant tree line: the lower foreground is brightest and likely within about 1–5 m, while the trees appear roughly 15–40 m away and the sky has no usable depth. The main person progresses from small and about 12–18 m ahead near the centre-left, to roughly 8–12 m ahead near centre, then about 4–7 m ahead on the right, and finally within approximately 1–3 m at the far right and partly outside the frame; this change is clearer than in RGB alone. Several other people remain much smaller near the tree line, roughly 20–35 m away and separated from the main person by around 10–25 m, but their depths are poorly resolved. The map supports near/far ordering and approach but not facing direction, gaze, or reliable arm's-reach judgments except that only the final main-person view may be near arm's reach; silhouettes bleed into the ground, vegetation has inconsistent values, and black regions should not be interpreted as measured distance.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map consistently isolates people from the grass, trees, and sky, revealing a main person ahead who shifts from centre-left to centre and then right while growing from a small full-body mask to a large mask clipped by the right edge. Relative to the RGB and apparent scale, this person is roughly 12–18 m away initially, about 8–12 m in the middle frames, about 4–7 m in frame 4, and around 1–3 m in frame 5; the other detected people remain approximately 20–35 m away near the horizon. The masks show that the main person is in front of the camera wearer and mostly unobstructed, while the final body is partly out of view; no person is clearly behind another, although distant figures partly merge with the dark background. The map makes small people easier to locate than RGB alone, but several masks and labels are tiny, fragmented, or truncated, no non-person objects are identified, and mask shape alone does not reliably establish gaze, exact facing direction, inter-person distance, or arm's reach.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely black across all five frames, so it provides no detected body or hand skeletons and therefore no direct evidence about limb positions, facing direction, gaze, reach, or person-to-person orientation. Using RGB context only, the main person moves from farther ahead near centre-left toward the camera's right side and becomes partly out of view in the last frame, but the absent skeleton prevents a pose-based estimate beyond the approximate RGB/depth distances of 12–18 m initially and 1–3 m finally. It also cannot spatially distinguish the smaller people near the tree line, estimate whether anyone's hands overlap another person or object, or reveal joints hidden by distance or cropping. Unlike a successful pose rendering, it adds nothing that is hard to see in RGB; its complete lack of detections is unreliable, especially for the close final person who should ordinarily provide the strongest visible body evidence.
